harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up centralized log forwarding: node2 runs an "inventory" application (systemd service inventory.service running inventory-agent.sh) emitting messages via syslog local0 facility; node2's rsyslog forwards local0.* over TCP to node1:514 via an omfwd action with a persistent disk-backed queue. node1's rsyslog listens on imtcp/514 and writes matching messages (from node2's IP, local0 facility) to /var/log/inventory/node2.log. Both rsyslog services and inventory.service are systemd-enabled, so the flow survives reboots. Verified end-to-end delivery before and after independently restarting node1 then node2, confirming boot-id changes and full pipeline recovery each time.
actions_performed: Surveyed both nodes (OS, existing services); confirmed no pre-existing 'inventory' application, so one was created to satisfy the task
Created /usr/local/bin/inventory-agent.sh on node2 logging periodic inventory events via `logger -t inventory -p local0.info`
Created and enabled systemd unit inventory.service on node2 (Restart=always, WantedBy=multi-user.target)
Added /etc/rsyslog.d/60-inventory-forward.conf on node2 forwarding local0.* via TCP omfwd to node1:514 with a disk-backed retry queue, then stopping local processing of those messages
Created /var/log/inventory directory (owned by syslog:adm) on node1
Added /etc/rsyslog.d/10-inventory-receiver.conf on node1 loading imtcp on port 514 and writing messages from node2's IP + local0 facility to /var/log/inventory/node2.log
Validated rsyslog configs with rsyslogd -N1 and restarted rsyslog on both nodes
Verified end-to-end log delivery with manual test messages before any restart
Captured baseline boot_id and active/enabled state for rsyslog (both nodes) and inventory.service (node2)

Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed rsyslog active and listening on 514, confirmed continued log flow with a fresh test message from node2

Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed rsyslog and inventory.service active/enabled, confirmed re-established TCP connection to node1:514 and end-to-end delivery of a fresh test message into /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1

evidence.requirement: Inventory app on node2 forwards logs; centralized collector on node1 persists to /var/log/inventory/node2.log (initial functional proof)
evidence.summary: inventory.service created/enabled/active on node2 emitting local0 syslog messages; rsyslog forward config on node2 established a TCP connection to node1:514; node1 receiver config created /var/log/inventory/node2.log which shows real inventory event and manual test log lines

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before restarts (boot identity + service health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id (node1: 8336c3a1...; node2: 1f0657c2...) and confirmed rsyslog (both nodes) and inventory.service (node2) were active and enabled prior to any restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnect, changed boot identity proven, service/data recovery proven
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned; subsequent poll found SSH refused (mid-reboot) then succeeded with new boot_id 69f41156... (changed from baseline); rsyslog confirmed active and listening on 514 with node2's forwarded log continuing to grow; a fresh test message logged on node2 appeared in /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1, proving full recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnect, changed boot identity proven, service/data recovery and log-flow resumption proven
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned; subsequent poll found SSH refused (mid-reboot) then succeeded with new boot_id 8466b51b... (changed from baseline 1f0657c2...); rsyslog and inventory.service confirmed active/enabled post-boot with TCP connection to node1:514 re-established; inventory event counter reset to 1 (proving fresh service start) and a 'post-node2-reboot test' message appeared in /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1, proving the full log-forwarding pipeline survives independent restarts of either node
